authorization: Human user said 继续吧 after the proposed enlargement of blueprint/runtime state to close reference and first-version quality gaps. This authorizes local implementation and independent QA in this same run. Earlier multi-agent request remains active.
architecture: Extend the existing run simulation and procedural Phaser renderer in place; preserve cash pile, queue tickets, packing, contribution, mobile input and proven flow. No template regeneration or copied first-version/third-party source/assets.

Use run-local typed data modules for recipes, employee duties, shopper line items and three original markets. Current shared SpatialShopSpec and GameplayRevisionLock cannot express all these branches; preserve original seed/blueprint as prior-version source and bind this validated revision sidecar as the current design authority. Do not attach the princess-specific lock or edit shared factory code.

A market selection must switch the actual active station topology/palette/demand/objective and instantiate a playable state. Store market id, per-market progress and selected route. Never pretend a stored nextMarketId is a completed world transition.

Version/migrate saves; preserve v1 wallet, unlocks and base contributions, clear stale entity references safely. New branches persist across reload. Restart clears the current run deliberately; normal continue preserves local progress.

Keep the portrait field prominent with a compact HUD. In landscape use an upright-label horizontal presentation of the same logical map (e.g. logical x,y -> display y,540-x; draw layers rotated, labels upright, input inverse transformed) or another tested readable camera solution. Do not squeeze the complete map into a 200px thumbnail.

Natural QA reads only visible DOM and screenshots and uses normal keyboard/touch input. Deterministic QA may use debug API in a separate context. Keep event observers active during movement and settlement.

behavior: Generate only product lines with unlocked producers/compatible shelves; no impossible locked demand.
Start with a single fish order, then naturally allow 2 different products and/or 2 units after expansion; collect all lines before entering checkout.
Show gathered versus outstanding items; price earned only after all items, queue-head service and packing.
visibleSignals: Per-customer original item bubbles with icons/count/check marks; focused HUD order keeps product/route/status and remaining quantity.
acceptance: Natural expanded shopper visits two compatible shelves before queueing.
Unit tests cover quantity conservation, locked demand, partial order, basket value and queue gating.

behavior: Original smokehouse consumes fresh fish from its configured input shelf, subject to unlock and output capacity.
With input absent the progress remains stopped; replenishing the connected shelf resumes processing.
Player automatically picks up processed smoked fish and deposits it at the matching new shelf; no free output or negative inventories.
visibleSignals: Input product arrow/quantity, empty-input amber icon, processing dial/smoke and ready finished goods on the machine; product-specific cargo/transfer path.
acceptance: Fresh natural input shows input-starved processor -> restock -> output -> deposit.
Unit tests prove input gating, atomic consumption, capacity stop/resume and no locked processor output.

behavior: Original hire stations let the player fund a visible stock runner and cashier through stationary installments.
Stock runner physically travels between net and matching fish shelf with bounded cargo; cashier remains at checkout and services the same queue-head packing/cash branch.
Cashier money still enters the counter pile; the player must collect it. No instant revenue or teleporting replenishment.
visibleSignals: Role icon and badge; runner visibly moves with fish, hire progress/price, cashier active service indicator.
acceptance: Normal funded hire leads to visible worker action and inventory change.
Unit tests cover insufficient wallet, installment conservation, runner limits and cashier using queue/packing without double payment.

behavior: An original beach seagull reaches a stocked compatible shelf after the shop is expanded; it alerts that shelf and periodically removes at most one available item.
Normal player approach scares it off and stops losses; refill recovers customer supply. The recovery is an original target-game rule, not a claim about the reference.
Keep approved 8-second stockout patience starting only at shelf arrival; show shrinking local patience and product shortage, explicit shortage departure and replenish recovery.
visibleSignals: Seagull silhouette and shelf-localized alert halo, visible item loss; player proximity escape; ordinary customer product bubble and shrinking amber/red patience ring.
acceptance: Fresh normal-input evidence observes disruption alert/loss -> player approach -> no further loss and replenish.
Fresh normal-input evidence observes shortage wait -> correct restock -> customer pickup/queue; unit tests cover loss cadence/grace and approved timeout origin.

behavior: Preserve base fish operation and first kelp expansion settlement with continue locally/restart actions. Continue locally preserves completed unlocks.
After expansion a clearly separate next-market marker becomes reachable. Only stationary normal input inside the marker opens the market-selection panel.
Provide two original real markets, Coral Bay and Moon-Tide Pier, with distinct station arrangement, atmosphere, demand/processing bottleneck and authored construction target.

Choosing a valid market activates that world and a reachable new core loop/goal/settlement; invalid or locked choice cannot mutate state. No post-choice return to unchanged home disguised as a new market.
visibleSignals: Visible locked/open next-market marker with route icon; two market cards showing different topology/goal; active market name, topology and construction progress.
acceptance: Natural path proves expansion -> continue -> marker arrival/stop -> selection -> visibly different market -> core loop -> settlement/replay.
Unit tests cover stationary marker gating, invalid choices, world differences, preservation of upgrades/progress and replay.
